headline: High risk of prompt-injection and cascading-error if slim’s shell/file outputs are fed into taipy workflows; data leakage and compliance risks are lower but non-zero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: slim can read/write filesystem artifacts and emits stdin/stdout plus broad network egress, so its outputs could be copied into taipy inputs or workflows. taipy has no documented isolation or provenance controls in the profile, so a shared file/workspace bridge is plausible. This is not proven by evidence, so I choose medium over low due to uncertainty.
conditions: IF slim output is copied into taipy-managed files or prompts
IF both agents share a workspace or message queue
IF taipy treats imported content as instructions or configuration
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct directories
Disable automatic ingestion of slim-generated files into taipy
Add a manual review step before taipy consumes slim output
Use read-only mounts for taipy inputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: slim touches certificate private keys, registry credentials, environment variables, and vulnerability data, while taipy’s profile does not show any data-handling limits. If they share a workspace, taipy could read sensitive artifacts produced by slim. The pairwise leakage path is plausible but not directly documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF slim writes secrets or certs into a shared directory
IF taipy reads that directory or ingests exported artifacts
IF sensitive artifacts are not redacted before handoff
mitigations: Store secrets in a separate vault path
Restrict taipy to a read-only sanitized export
Rotate any credentials exposed in shared artifacts
Delete temporary files after slim finishes
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: slim has unrestricted filesystem write, shell execution, subprocesses, and broad network egress; taipy is a data-engineering app with no concurrency controls documented. Even without explicit overlap in taipy’s write surface, shared mutable resources or files can conflict. Because the profiles do not prove locking, I escalate to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory
IF taipy mutates shared job state or files
IF no external lock serializes access
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Serialize writes with a simple lock file
Run one agent at a time on shared resources
Check for stale temp files before starting
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: slim can generate container-analysis outputs and taipy can orchestrate data workflows, so a plausible pathway is slim output becoming taipy input without verification. The profiles do not show taipy critically validating upstream results, and no evidence bundle exists to prove safeguards. That makes a default medium-risk cascading error more likely than low.
conditions: IF taipy consumes slim-produced reports or artifacts
IF taipy uses those artifacts as authoritative inputs
IF no validation step checks schema or freshness
mitigations: Require schema validation on slim outputs
Add a checksum or signature check before taipy ingests data
Insert a human review gate for high-impact actions
Log and compare upstream assumptions before execution
requires-engineering: implement typed contracts between agents

E_compliance.rationale: slim explicitly handles registry credentials, certificate private keys, environment variables, and vulnerability data, which can create residency and retention obligations. taipy’s profile gives no compliance controls or retention policy, so if the pair processes regulated data in a shared workflow, mismatch risk exists. I cite only slim because the compliance-sensitive data classes are documented there; taipy lacks such fields.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed through slim-generated artifacts
IF taipy stores or logs those artifacts beyond the intended retention window
IF no DPA or residency control is configured for the workflow
mitigations: Avoid routing regulated data through shared artifacts
Set a short retention window for intermediate files
Redact secrets before export from slim
Confirm storage region for any taipy persistence
requires-engineering: document and enforce data-handling policy
